values.description: Participants and capability bindings, seeded by bin/setup.py. HOST ONLY: the API base is /api/v1, so a request spells it out. REGISTRY_PORT in .env.
The consumer adapter's network identity, and what its signatures verify against. CONSUMER_SUBSCRIBER_ID in .env.

The address PEERS are told to POST to, published in the registry row. Nothing in this stack resolves it, so a wrong value costs nothing locally and everything on a shared network -- and the registry cannot correct it. CONSUMER_BASE_URL in .env.

EMPTY ON PURPOSE. The public half lives in quick-start/keys/keys.json, which bin/setup.py generates; paste it in before registering. setup.py has already registered this participant, so it is normally not needed.
IMD Mausamgram, the weather upstream. Half of its binding key. MAUSAMGRAM_PARTICIPANT_ID in .env.
<participant-id>|<capability>. Used to look up the binding's osid. The provider adapter builds this from the incoming payload, so it must match the registry row exactly -- a mismatch is a 404.
What the binding row publishes and the provider adapter fetches. A TAG ref, so what a running stack reads is fixed at 0.0.1 and a later push does not move it. MAUSAMGRAM_MAPPING_URL in .env.

WHICH CAPABILITY THE 3. Capability Schemas FOLDER OPERATES ON -- the one variable to change to work on another, because the schemaUrl and the display name are derived from it rather than written down. The four this deployment serves are openagrinet:WeatherObservation, openagrinet:MandiPrice, openagrinet:KnowledgeAdvisory and openagrinet:AgricultureFacility; network-specs carries four more packs no capability uses yet.

The pack version, and the row's version field. All eight packs are v0.1 today. Per capability in setup.py rather than one setting for all four, because a capability can move to v0.2 while the others stay -- so if you point capability-code at one that has, change this too.
